 Supporting teachers for learning continuity in flood-affected areas in Nepal
 For children whose schooling was disrupted by the floods, returning to learning also means receiving support to cope with what they have experienced. Initial reports indicate that more than 14,000 children had their learning disrupted when the Bhote Koshi flood struck Nepal on 26 August 2026. Save the Children 5 November 2026 To help teachers respond to these learners’ needs, UNESCO organized a three-day training on Education in Emergencies and Psychosocial Support from 13 to 15 October 2026, in partnership with Save the Children International, Gajuri Rural Municipality, Benighat Rorang Rural Municipality and local partner Focus Nepal. The training directly supported teachers from flood-affected communities, with the aim of helping them maintain learning and support their students’ well-being. 
 The 28 participants included 24 teachers and resource teachers from Gajuri Rural Municipality and 4 teachers from Benighat Rorang Rural Municipality. They described the training as practical and responsive to the needs of schools and communities recovering from the floods. 
 Save the children The training covered practical approaches to maintaining learning during emergencies and supporting students through psychosocial support, socio-emotional learning and basic counselling. It also addressed teachers’ own psychosocial well-being and their role in disaster preparedness, emergency response and recovery in the education sector. 
 Sunita Khatiwada, Head of the Education Section of Gajuri Rural Municipality, who inaugurated the workshop, described it as timely and relevant to strengthening schools’ preparedness and response capacities. 
 Further support remains necessary to help flood-affected children continue their education and receive psychosocial support. While much more remains to be done to ensure that education and learning continue for learners in the affected areas, it is equally urgent that educators are well equipped and skilled to tackle challenges during such times. 
 This intervention was supported through the Education in Emergencies (EiE) allocation of UNESCO’ SDG 4 Emergency Fund , which aims to strengthen education resilience and support affected learners in crisis contexts.
